items.rationale: I_current_Chr_Max bounds the charge acceptance of the cell chemistry and the current rating of the DC contactors and busbars.
items.text: While the battery system is in the Charging state, the battery system shall limit the DC charging current to not more than {I_current_Chr_Max}.
items.title: Maximum DC charging current

items.rationale: Coulomb counting is the stakeholder-selected SOC mechanism. Fixing the estimator lets drift, reset and recalibration behaviour be specified against it.
items.text: The battery system shall determine the technical state of charge by integrating the measured DC current over time.
items.title: Technical state of charge by coulomb counting

items.rationale: Reserving the lower 25 % and the upper 10 % of the technical window protects cell life and guarantees a reserve the customer cannot deplete. The clamp is required because the stakeholder mapping is undefined outside 25 % to 90 %.
items.text: The battery system shall derive the customer state of charge from the technical state of charge by a linear mapping in which a technical state of charge of {SOC_tech_at_cust_0pct} yields a customer state of charge of 0 % and a technical state of charge of {SOC_tech_at_cust_100pct} yields a customer state of charge of 100 %, clamped to the range 0 % to 100 %.
items.title: Customer state of charge derivation

items.rationale: OCV-based SOC recalibration is valid only once diffusion transients have decayed. t_transient_Voltage_sec bounds how long the system must wait before trusting an OCV reading.
items.text: When the battery system enters the Sleep state, the battery terminal voltage shall converge to the open-circuit voltage within {t_transient_Voltage_sec}.
items.title: Terminal voltage relaxation to open-circuit voltage

items.rationale: Sleep is the only window in which no load current masks the cell-to-cell spread, and balancing there avoids spending traction energy on equalisation.
items.text: While the battery system is in the Sleep state, the battery system shall equalise the cell voltages by the active discharge mechanism.
items.title: Cell balancing while sleeping

items.rationale: Udc_min and Udc_Max are the interface limits the inverter and the DC charger are rated for. Leaving the band risks both cell damage and downstream converter damage.
items.text: The battery system shall maintain the battery terminal voltage within the range {Udc_min} to {Udc_Max}.
items.title: Terminal voltage operating range

items.rationale: T_batt_max is the onset of accelerated ageing and, beyond it, of thermal runaway risk. It is the ceiling every thermal mitigation is designed to hold.
items.text: The battery system shall limit the battery temperature to not more than {T_batt_max}.
items.title: Battery temperature ceiling

items.rationale: Ramping current to zero across T_batt_safety_threshold approaches the ceiling asymptotically instead of tripping a hard cut-off, which would be both a drivability and a contactor-wear problem.
items.text: While the battery temperature is not less than {T_batt_max} minus {T_batt_safety_threshold} and not more than {T_batt_max}, the battery system shall apply to the actual charging current limit a derating factor that decreases linearly from 1,0 to 0,0 across that band.
items.title: Charging current derating near the temperature ceiling

items.rationale: A three-step heater is specified rather than a continuous one because the traction battery heater is switched by relays, so only discrete power levels are realisable.
items.text: The battery system shall provide the heater states 0, 1 and 2, corresponding to the heater being off, the heater operating at {P_heater_middle} and the heater operating at {P_heater_max}.
items.title: Heater power states

items.rationale: Below T_batt_min the cells cannot accept charge without lithium plating, so the fastest available recovery to the permitted window takes precedence over heater energy use.
items.text: If the battery temperature is below {T_batt_min}, then the battery system shall command heater state 2.
items.title: Heater at maximum power below the minimum temperature
